options.text: The enzyme reacts with water to convert all nitrogen atoms into ammonia gas
options.mistakeAnalysis: Student miscalculated or applied wrong principle

options.text: Denaturation destroys the substrate molecules before they can bind
options.mistakeAnalysis: Student miscalculated or applied wrong principle

options.text: All peptide bonds in the enzyme backbone are hydrolysed within milliseconds
options.mistakeAnalysis: Student miscalculated or applied wrong principle

options.text: The loss of tertiary and secondary folding disrupts the precise three-dimensional geometry of the catalytic active site
options.mistakeAnalysis: Follows standard NCERT derivation and principle

detailedSolution: An enzyme's catalytic activity is strictly dependent on its precise three-dimensional tertiary conformation, which positions specific catalytic amino acid residues together to form an active site. Denaturation unfolds this conformation, destroying the active site geometry so it can no longer bind or convert substrates, leading to total loss of biological activity.

questionText: Vitamins are divided into two main categories based on solubility. Which of the following sets contains ONLY fat-soluble vitamins?

options.text: Vitamins B1, B2, B6, and C
options.mistakeAnalysis: Student miscalculated or applied wrong principle

options.text: Vitamins B12, C, D, and K
options.mistakeAnalysis: Student miscalculated or applied wrong principle

options.text: Vitamins A, B1, C, and E
options.mistakeAnalysis: Student miscalculated or applied wrong principle

options.text: Vitamins A, D, E, and K
options.mistakeAnalysis: Follows standard NCERT derivation and principle

detailedSolution: Vitamins are classified into: (1) Fat-soluble vitamins, which are soluble in fats and organic oils but insoluble in water: Vitamins A, D, E, and K. They are stored in the liver and adipose tissues. (2) Water-soluble vitamins, which dissolve in water: B-group vitamins and Vitamin C.
